sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier labrum nearly oval, wide; mandibles rather short, acute and curved at the apex, the base of the right mandible with two fairly small teeth, the left mandible with three teeth; antenna 15-segmented, segment 3 nearly as long as segments 4 and 5 and slightly shorter than segment 2. The wide oval labrum and the tridentate left mandible are the characters that separate it from L. orthocephalus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: labrum nearly oval, wide. Mandibles rather short, acute and curved at the apex; the base of the right mandible with two fairly small teeth, the left mandible with three teeth. Antenna 15-segmented, segment 3 nearly as long as segments 4 and 5 and slightly shorter than segment 2. Measurements: body length 9 mm.

note: Adapted from Silvestri's 1901 "Nota preliminare sui Termitidi sud-americani" (in Latin), where the species was named Cornitermes laticephalus sp. n. and only brief diagnostic characters of the soldier and the body length were given; type locality Coxipò (Cuyabá), Brazil. Snyder (1949) made it the type species of the genus Paracornitermes; it is now mostly placed in Labiotermes.
